{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
    "line": 119,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Dereferences undefined destination calendar for Google Meet fallback",
    "body": "`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` produces `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty. The next line accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, so any booking with `MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar throws a TypeError during event creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== \"google_calendar\"` or guard the value."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 254,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Google update event selects no calendar when externalCalendarId is missing",
    "body": "In `updateEvent`, the else branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then executes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That compares `cal.externalId` to null/undefined and normally returns undefined, so `calendar.events.update` receives `calendarId: undefined`. Rescheduling or updating a Google event without a stored `externalCalendarId` fails. The selection should look up the destination for the current credential/first destination, with a primary fallback."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 315,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Google delete event can fall back to primary for secondary calendars",
    "body": "In `deleteEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is null the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since the find predicate compares to null/undefined, it normally returns undefined, so `calendarId` falls back to `\"primary\"`. For events originally created on a secondary calendar but whose reference has no `externalCalendarId`, this deletes from the wrong calendar or misses the real event. The destination should be resolved by credential or first destination, not by comparing with the missing ID."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 168,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Google Meet hangout patch uses undefined calendarId on primary fallback",
    "body": "`createEvent` inserts with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || \"primary\"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credentialId, `selectedCalendar` is undefined even though the event was created on primary, so the patch is sent with an undefined calendar ID and can fail. The patch should use the same `selectedCalendar || \"primary\"` fallback."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts",
    "line": 1077,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar",
    "body": "`evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor organizer has one. Later, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`, so host calendars are silently discarded. For collective events where the organizer lacks a calendar but hosts have configured calendars, no events are created for the hosts. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to `[]` before the push, or assign `[...teamDestinationCalendars]` explicitly."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts",
    "line": 454,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Recurring cancellation only deletes first calendar reference per booking",
    "body": "In the recurring cancellation branch, for every updated booking the code uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes(\"_calendar\"))`. With multiple calendar references (the newly supported multi-host case), only the first reference is selected; the loop then tries that same UID against every calendar credential. The remaining host calendar events for each recurring booking are never deleted, leaving ghost events after cancellation. The code should iterate all calendar references and use each reference's own credentialId/type/externalCalendarId."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 73,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Office 365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar",
    "body": "`createEvent` destructures only `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` from the array and does not know which destination the current EventManager loop iteration is targeting. When a collective event has multiple Office 365 host calendars, every Office 365 credential creates the event in the first host's calendar instead of its own. This service needs to select the destination matching the current credential, similar to the Google implementation, or otherwise receive the current destination external ID."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 128,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar",
    "body": "`createEvent` only reads `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses that calendar ID. EventManager now invokes createEvent for each host destination, but the same full `destinationCalendar` array is passed every time and the service does not select the current credential's destination. For collective events with multiple Lark-calendar hosts, each event is created on the first host's Lark calendar rather than the correct host's calendar."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts",
    "line": 151,
    "severity": "critical",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Organization slug condition was inverted",
    "body": "The previous logic used `!(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED) && { slug }`, meaning the Team/org got a `slug` when team billing was not enabled. This PR changes it to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, so the slug is only set when billing is enabled and omitted when it is disabled. The `requestedSlug` metadata change at line 153 is similarly inverted. This changes organization creation behavior based on the billing flag and can break subdomain/org provisioning."
  }
]}

findings.title: Dereferences undefined destination calendar for Google Meet fallback
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` produces `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty. The next line accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, so any booking with `MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar throws a TypeError during event creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` or guard the value.

findings.title: Google update event selects no calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
findings.body: In `updateEvent`, the else branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then executes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That compares `cal.externalId` to null/undefined and normally returns undefined, so `calendar.events.update` receives `calendarId: undefined`. Rescheduling or updating a Google event without a stored `externalCalendarId` fails. The selection should look up the destination for the current credential/first destination, with a primary fallback.

findings.title: Google delete event can fall back to primary for secondary calendars
findings.body: In `deleteEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is null the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since the find predicate compares to null/undefined, it normally returns undefined, so `calendarId` falls back to `"primary"`. For events originally created on a secondary calendar but whose reference has no `externalCalendarId`, this deletes from the wrong calendar or misses the real event. The destination should be resolved by credential or first destination, not by comparing with the missing ID.

findings.title: Google Meet hangout patch uses undefined calendarId on primary fallback
findings.body: `createEvent` inserts with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credentialId, `selectedCalendar` is undefined even though the event was created on primary, so the patch is sent with an undefined calendar ID and can fail. The patch should use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` fallback.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor organizer has one. Later, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`, so host calendars are silently discarded. For collective events where the organizer lacks a calendar but hosts have configured calendars, no events are created for the hosts. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to `[]` before the push, or assign `[...teamDestinationCalendars]` explicitly.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation only deletes first calendar reference per booking
findings.body: In the recurring cancellation branch, for every updated booking the code uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. With multiple calendar references (the newly supported multi-host case), only the first reference is selected; the loop then tries that same UID against every calendar credential. The remaining host calendar events for each recurring booking are never deleted, leaving ghost events after cancellation. The code should iterate all calendar references and use each reference's own credentialId/type/externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Office 365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: `createEvent` destructures only `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` from the array and does not know which destination the current EventManager loop iteration is targeting. When a collective event has multiple Office 365 host calendars, every Office 365 credential creates the event in the first host's calendar instead of its own. This service needs to select the destination matching the current credential, similar to the Google implementation, or otherwise receive the current destination external ID.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: `createEvent` only reads `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses that calendar ID. EventManager now invokes createEvent for each host destination, but the same full `destinationCalendar` array is passed every time and the service does not select the current credential's destination. For collective events with multiple Lark-calendar hosts, each event is created on the first host's Lark calendar rather than the correct host's calendar.

findings.title: Organization slug condition was inverted
findings.body: The previous logic used `!(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED) && { slug }`, meaning the Team/org got a `slug` when team billing was not enabled. This PR changes it to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, so the slug is only set when billing is enabled and omitted when it is disabled. The `requestedSlug` metadata change at line 153 is similarly inverted. This changes organization creation behavior based on the billing flag and can break subdomain/org provisioning.
